scope: Manual review against the synthetic scenario. These expectations are never sent to the answering model.
common: Answer the whole request and respect network, route, station, vehicle and time scope.
Use successful retrieved evidence for current or historical claims; retain units and denominators.
Keep scheduled service, predictions, vehicle positions, observed passages and passenger counts distinct.
Keep a reported cause within its stated scope. Hypotheses require evidence and remain hypotheses.
Provide useful conditional work when a required integration is absent, without inventing its output.
Give staff a clear priority or next step; no raw JSON, capability catalogue or unnecessary refusal.

ratings.acceptable: Addresses the essential request with supported facts, appropriate limits and a useful operational next step. This is one scenario result, not production validation.
ratings.partial: Useful supported content, but a material requested part is missing or the scope/qualification needs correction. No invented decisive cause, forecast or action benefit.
ratings.fail: Wrong entity/scope, invented decisive fact, invalid operational recommendation, unsupported causal/history claim, or no usable answer.

cases.expect: Assess all seven routes: late predictions on 39, 55, 57, 66; matching reports on 1, 9, Red; cancellation/gap on 66 and Route 39 construction. Reporting coverage is not service health.

Surface network exceptions beyond the selected Route 39, including 66 cancellation/full occupancy, close/wide spacing and the separate accessibility notice. Do not claim a historical anomaly baseline.
Use shared directed stop connections for geographic overlap across routes; do not invent street congestion, terminal onset or a shared construction cause.

For 66 identify one late comparison, three matching comparisons, one cancellation, wider spacing and reported full occupancy. Distinguish plausible capacity/spacing mechanisms from unknown traffic, dwell or dispatch causes.

Resolve vehicle 1827, not route 1827. Its next compared departure has +20 minutes. Three forecasts for Harvard Square change from +10 to +15 to +20; they do not establish where or when actual delay began.
No trip is selected. Clarify its identity; do not silently pick the worst Route 39 trip. Block/relief/connection propagation is unavailable without assignment and transfer evidence.
Inspect both close and wide spacing across the network; do not call the 25-minute Route 66 gap bunching. Repeated comparisons of the same trip pair are not multiple vehicle pairs.
Locate a predicted 25-minute Route 66 gap versus 10 scheduled minutes. Describe possible rider waiting without claiming every rider waits 25 minutes or all future service is known.
Verify the asserted 35-minute gap at selected Harvard Square; do not adopt an unsupported premise. Separate confirmed cancellation on 66 from absent reports and unknown dispatch/short-turn actions.
Query Red Line historical evidence; this scenario has no weekly baseline. Today's matching predictions cannot answer weekly reliability or rider experience.
Inspect Harvard Square and related routes, distinguish current spatial overlap from retained prediction changes, and leave actual incident onset unestablished.
Inspect 39, 55 and 57 together. Shared delay locations support investigation; only 39 has a construction notice. Simultaneous onset or construction on all three is unestablished.
Treat the crash as a user-reported condition near the selected location. Identify scheduled exposure separately from blocked geometry, actual vehicle traversal and unknown passenger counts.
Distinguish 30/60/90-minute scheduled exposure from a calibrated future-state forecast. Future trips need not report yet. Do not invent recovery or worsening trajectories.
Treat 4:20 clearance as hypothetical, not notice expiry or a recovery promise. Explain recovery dependencies and request the service/location/clock needed for a calculation.
Compare hold, short turn, express, extra vehicle and no intervention conditionally. Include onboard delay, gap ahead, skipped-stop coverage and resource feasibility; no unsupported hold duration.
Identify the unspecified bus and turn feasibility. Discuss improvement on the served side and lost service beyond the turn; no simulated wait changes or claim a live simulation ran.
Identify the three intended routes and spare locations/crews/capacity. Use gap and occupancy evidence as triage, not a fabricated optimal assignment or passenger-benefit calculation.
Missing connection protection data include arriving and departing services, transfer allowance, onward interval and onboard consequences. Do not infer feasible holds from a route delay alone.
One Route 66 vehicle reports FULL alongside degraded spacing; no APC/AFC counts or demand baseline establish excess demand, crush loads or the direction of causality.
No fleet readiness or pull-out assignment integration exists. Request available/defect/assigned/spare vehicles and the PM timetable; current reporting vehicles cannot establish PM fleet adequacy.
No crew roster, relief times or duty assignments exist. Identify the needed relief record and compare planned handoff to predicted arrival only after the operator/trip is known.

Do not authorize continued service from GTFS or invented fault diagnostics. Request actual fault codes and maintenance/dispatch assessment; outline a swap/coverage decision without declaring the vehicle safe.

Use selected Harvard Square scope. Park Street elevator maintenance is an access notice, not evidence of Harvard Square running delay. Do not turn Route 39 construction into a stationwide infrastructure cause.

Clarify the sign/baseline of 14-minute deviation as needed. A longer interval increases possible waiting and accumulation; it is not 14 extra minutes for each rider. Any half-headway example needs explicit steady/random-arrival assumptions.
Establish actual A/B endpoints and suspended segment before routing. This fixture has no routing adapter; do not invent itineraries, active closure avoidance or accessible alternatives.
Produce all three requested channel drafts with route/location, supported disruption and apology. No invented cause, recovery deadline, accessibility guarantee or publishing claim.

Read the notice and compare its scope with the observed condition. Distinguish Route 39 disruption from other routes and separate elevator access; identify missing direction/stop/alternative information without inventing it.
Check actual feed age, trip matching and available cross-source corroboration. Freshness is not prediction accuracy; absence of APC/dispatch data prevents those cross-checks.

Retrieve yesterday's retained evidence, which is absent. Do not retell today's snapshot as yesterday or claim causal effects of unrecorded interventions. Specify an event/action/outcome reconstruction.

Combine Route 39 delay/spacing, scoped Huntington Avenue notice, potential rider effects and useful next investigation. Do not invent outbound direction, onset, accident, terminal pull-out or passenger counts.

Use current morning evidence only as a PM preparation watchlist. Identify the missing PM readiness and forecast information; no assumption current gaps persist all day or unreported future trips have no assigned vehicles.
